property_summary: For every call, C.version() returns a 3-component semantic version string with major, minor, and patch separated by two '.' characters (e.g. "x.y.z"); the mutant that returns "1.0" violates this by returning only two components for some inputs.
Only the depositor account can successfully call setL1BlockValues (calls revert for other senders).

For any caller address provided as the depositorAccount, the correct contract allows setL1BlockValues to succeed when msg.sender == depositorAccount (the externally settable variable), whereas the mutant instead only allows the hardcoded DEPOSITOR_ACCOUNT, so there exist caller addresses for which the reference accepts calls but the mutant rejects them.

For every caller address x set into depositorAccount, calling setL1BlockValues from x succeeds on the reference C (which checks msg.sender == depositorAccount) — the mutant that instead requires msg.sender == DEPOSITOR_ACCOUNT will reject calls for some x, so there exists an address input (the fuzzed depositor) for which the reference allows the call but the mutant reverts.

For every caller address set into the contract's public depositorAccount variable, calling setL1BlockValues from that same address should succeed on the reference contract; the mutant instead only permits the hardcoded DEPOSITOR_ACCOUNT, causing calls from other depositorAccount values to revert.

For any address A stored into c.depositorAccount, calling setL1BlockValues from A always succeeds on the reference contract (which checks msg.sender == depositorAccount); the mutant which instead requires msg.sender == DEPOSITOR_ACCOUNT will reject (revert) for some fuzzed depositorAccount addresses that differ from the hardcoded DEPOSITOR_ACCOUNT.
